gaps.sentence: 'I'll finish the report today,' she said. She said she would finish the report ___.
gaps.explanation: Today becomes that day when reported later.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'You should apply for the grant,' he told me. He ___ me to apply for the grant.
gaps.explanation: Advice is reported as advise + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
gaps.explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

gaps.sentence: 'Get out of my way!' the guard snapped. The guard snapped at me ___ out of my way.
gaps.hint: snap at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The order is reported as snapped at me + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Let's walk to the launch instead of driving,' he said. He ___ to the launch instead of driving.
gaps.explanation: 'Suggest' takes a gerund, never a to-infinitive.
